input: matrix is a nonempty rectangular binary matrix with 1 <= rows, columns <= 300. Rows may alias because the input is read-only. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Largest number of rows that can each become constant after one shared set of column flips; constant rows may have different constant bits.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: A row and its complement have the same collision-free, fixed-length relative-to-first-bit key. Precisely those rows can all be made individually constant by the same flips. Frequencies and the answer are at most the row count. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: With R rows and C columns: expected O(R*C) time and O(R*C) auxiliary storage, including all stored string keys, hash/equality work proportional to key length, temporary character arrays and joins. Hash maps assume expected constant overhead apart from key processing. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 445 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source.
